newsitem.title: BRAZIL: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN TAKES POLE, BEATTIE OUT FOR SEASON.
newsitem.headline: MOTORCYCLING-DOOHAN TAKES POLE, BEATTIE OUT FOR SEASON.

text.p: Michael Doohan, who has already sewn up the world 500 cc motorcycling championship, took pole position on the eve of Sunday's Brazilian Grand Prix.
Fellow Australian Darryl Beattie's injury-hit season came to an end with complications of the broken wrist which kept him out for 17 weeks of this championship campaign.

Doohan, who claimed his third successive world title in the category by finishing second in last month's Catalunia Grand Prix, claimed his ninth pole of the season with a time of one minute 53.293 seconds.
He then criticised the Jacarepagua circuit on the outskirts of Rio de Janeiro as being too bumpy.

"We haven't really tried ajusting the bike because basically it's so bumpy that there's nothing you can do. You have to let the bumps do what they want to the bike," said Doonhan, who will be aiming for his first win in Brazil.
"The bumps are very unpredictable. It's almost scary in some points."
Beattie, runner-up to Doohan last year and third in 1993, withdrew because of more complications to the wrist injury which has kept him out for most of the season, his team Lucky Strike Suzuki said.
He will also miss the Australian Grand Prix in two weeks' time, the last race of the season.
X-ray photographs, taken after he complained of pain during practice on Friday, showed that a piece of bone was floating in his wrist, something which had not showed up on previous X-rays.
Beattie, who finished 18th in Friday's practice, had only ridden in the Catalunia race three weeks ago since breaking his wrist in an accident during practice for the French grand prix.
He had also missed the first two races of the season after suffering concussion in a pre-season testing accident.
